Assuming "create an app" = an installable app on iPhone/iPad/desktop built from the existing React code (PWA first, Capacitor shell second), not a rewrite in Swift or React Native. Section 2 compares the options so you can overrule that.
Ask 1 · Responsive
## One codebase, three form factors
Today Forge is a phone app that happens to open on bigger screens. The fix is not three layouts — it is one shell that changes its navigation pattern and column count based on container width, plus an input model that stops assuming a mouse or a finger.
## What the audit found
Blocks desktop / iPad today
.app { max-width: 640px } and .tab-bar-inner { max-width: 640px } — on a 1440px monitor Forge is a 640px strip; on an iPad Pro it is a phone column with dead margins.
1 @media rule in 1,139 lines of CSS (prefers-reduced-motion). 0 width breakpoints.
20+ :hover rules with no (hover: hover) guard → hover state sticks after a tap on iPad.
No :focus-visible styles → keyboard / Magic Keyboard users get browser defaults only.
FAB offset is calc(64px + safe-area) — hard-codes the tab-bar height, so it breaks the moment nav moves to a side rail.
DSA Mastery Map is a separate 8,320-line page outside the shell, with its own layout.
Already right — keep
viewport-fit=cover + env(safe-area-inset-*) on the shell and tab bar.
100dvh app height (survives iOS Safari toolbar collapse).
CSS custom-property tokens + data-accent themes → theming is already centralised.
prefers-reduced-motion honoured.
Tabs are code-split (lazy()) → desktop adds panes, not weight.
Local-first store → a second device is just another client of the same sync path.
## Design rule: by container width and input type, never by device name
iPad windows can be anywhere from a ~320px Slide Over to a 1366px full screen, and rotate live. A "tablet layout" keyed to iPad is wrong half the time; a layout keyed to available width is right all the time.
Width (container) | Typical | Navigation | Content columns | Density / input |
< 600 | iPhone, iPad Slide Over / ⅓ Split | Bottom tab bar (5 tabs), FAB | 1 — list → push detail as sheet | 44px targets, thumb-zone actions, sheets for forms |
600 – 1023 | iPad portrait, iPad ½ Split, small laptop window | 72px icon rail (left) | 1–2 — list, cards flow 2-up; detail as side sheet | Touch-first (44px) but hover-safe; pointer + keyboard supported |
1024 – 1279 | iPad landscape, laptop | 220px labelled sidebar | 2 — master list + detail pane | Keyboard shortcuts visible, (hover:hover) affordances only if fine pointer |
≥ 1280 | Desktop, iPad Pro 13" landscape | Sidebar + command palette (⌘K) | 3 — list · detail · inspector (stats, notes, Pencil) | Dense rows (36px), multi-select, drag-drop between panes |
## Live adaptive shell
Drag the slider (or pick a preset). This is a real container-query layout — the same markup, no JS layout logic. Watch the nav move from bottom tabs → rail → sidebar and the content go 1 → 2 → 3 panes.
Width
## Shell CSS to drop in
/* container = the app root, so Split View / Slide Over / resized desktop windows all work */
.app-root { container: app / inline-size; min-height: 100dvh; }
.shell { display: grid; grid-template-rows: 1fr auto; } /* phone: content + bottom tabs */
.nav-rail, .nav-side { display: none; }
@container app (min-width: 600px) {
.shell { grid-template-columns: 72px 1fr; grid-template-rows: 1fr; } /* tablet: rail */
.tabs { display: none; } .nav-rail { display: flex; }
}
@container app (min-width: 1024px) {
.shell { grid-template-columns: 220px 1fr; } /* sidebar + master/detail */
.nav-rail { display: none; } .nav-side { display: flex; }
.page { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(320px, 400px) 1fr; }
}
@container app (min-width: 1280px) { .page { grid-template-columns: 360px 1fr 300px; } }
/* input model */
@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) { .row:hover { background: var(--hover); } }
@media (pointer: coarse) { .btn, .row { min-height: 44px; } }
:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
.fab { bottom: calc(var(--tabbar-h, 0px) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + 16px); } /* var set to 0 when rail/sidebar active */
Tabs become routes (/life/tasks) so desktop panes, iPad windows and deep links share one URL scheme — today tabs are component state with no router.
## How we will know it works
Playwright project | Viewport | Must assert |
iPhone 14 | 390×844, touch | bottom tabs visible; no horizontal scroll; FAB clears tab bar + home indicator |
iPad 11" portrait | 834×1194, touch | rail visible, tabs hidden; no sticky hover; targets ≥ 44px |
iPad 11" landscape | 1194×834, touch | sidebar + 2 panes; rotate mid-session keeps selected item |
iPad Split ⅓ | ~375×1024 | falls back to phone shell (container query, not device) |
Desktop Chrome | 1440×900, mouse | 3 panes; ⌘K opens palette; Tab order and focus ring visible |
Ask 2a · The app
## From web page to installable app — and what has to change underneath
Forge is already local-first with cloud sync, which is the hard 70% of an app. What is missing is delivery (install, offline shell, native hooks), a sync model that survives two devices editing the same list, and a shell that scales past a phone.
## 2.1 Which kind of "app"?
Option | Reuses today's React code | Install on iPhone / iPad | Native hooks | Effort (solo) | Verdict |
PWA (add service worker) | ~100% | Add to Home Screen; Web Push needs iOS 16.4+ and an installed app | Pointer Events incl. Apple Pencil pressure; no Keychain, no widgets | S | Phase 1 — ship first |
Capacitor (WKWebView shell) | ~95% | TestFlight / App Store (Apple Developer Program, $99/yr) | APNs, Keychain, haptics, share sheet via plugins; widgets need a Swift extension | M | Phase 3 — iOS + iPadOS |
Tauri 2 (desktop) | ~95% | n/a (desktop); mobile targets exist but are younger | Tray, global shortcuts, file system | M | Optional — desktop PWA install covers most of it |
React Native / Expo | ~30% (logic only, UI rewritten) | App Store | Fully native views | L | Only if native UI feel matters more than velocity |
SwiftUI native | 0% UI | App Store | Best Pencil / widgets / Live Activities | XL | Skip — Apple-only, second codebase |
One React build, three delivery shells. The only per-platform code is the thin adapter layer on the right — storage, notifications, haptics and pencil input — which is why Phase 1 comes before any App Store work.
## 2.2 High-level design
Solid boxes exist today. dashed = new Moving dots show the three live paths: local → cloud writes, cloud → other device, LLM calls.
Reads and writes never wait on the network: the UI talks to store.js/IndexedDB, and the sync engine moves data in the background. The serverless proxy exists only for things the browser cannot do safely (hold the Groq key, bypass Codeforces CORS).

## 2.4 Reconcile rule, and where it loses data
This is decideSync() from src/sync/logic.js. It is correct and well tested — for one writer per key at a time. Two devices editing different tasks in the same list fall into the "newer wins" branch and one edit disappears.
The decision runs on boot and on every Realtime event. The unit of comparison is the whole key (tasks, habits, expenses…) — that granularity is the weakness, not the logic.
Weak points of sync v1
Lost edits: phone renames task A offline, laptop adds task B offline → whichever syncs last overwrites the other's whole list. Try it in Lab 1 →
Payload grows with history: every keystroke-level save re-uploads the entire expenses blob; a year of spends is pushed to change one row.
Clock trust: Date.now() from each device decides the winner; a phone with a wrong clock silently wins forever.
No history: no way to see or undo "what did sync overwrite?" beyond the one-time __pre_sync_backup.
Sync v2 — per-record rows, same LWW idea, finer grain
create table tasks (
id uuid primary key,
user_id uuid not null references auth.users,
body jsonb not null,
updated_at timestamptz not null, -- server clock wins ties
deleted_at timestamptz, -- tombstone, not DELETE
device_id text not null,
rev bigint generated always as identity
);
-- same shape for habits, expenses, loans, goals, notes…
-- client pulls "where rev > last_seen_rev" (cheap delta)
## 2.5 Frontend architecture
Dependencies point down only. Domain logic stays pure (it is what node --test covers today); the platform adapter is the one seam where the web build and the Capacitor build differ.
## 2.6 Decisions and what they cost
Decision | Why | Cost / risk | Reversible? |
PWA first, Capacitor second | Reuses 100% of the code; proves responsive + offline before paying for an Apple account | iOS Safari has no Background Sync; Web Push only for installed apps | Yes |
Keep Supabase (Auth + Postgres + Realtime) | Already wired, RLS gives per-user isolation without a custom backend | Free projects pause after about a week idle → add a keep-alive and a periodic JSON export | Mostly — it is plain Postgres |
Sync v2: per-record rows + tombstones, still LWW | Removes the lost-edit class of bug for a single user on 2–3 devices | One-time migration from kv_store; more rows; schema per entity | Partly (keep kv_store as backup) |
No CRDT yet | Hybrid logical clock + per-record LWW is enough for one user | Revisit for collaborative notes or per-stroke Pencil data | Yes |
Container queries + one route per screen | Correct in Split View / Slide Over; deep links and desktop panes share URLs | Needs a tiny router; tab state refactor | Yes |
LLM stays behind /api/agent (owner-gated) | An app bundle is inspectable — a key in a Capacitor build is a leaked key | Extra hop; add SSE streaming later | Yes |
Platform adapter interface | Web and Capacitor implement the same storage / notify / haptics / pencil contract | Small up-front abstraction | Yes |
## 2.7 Build order rough solo estimate — not a commitment

Ask 3 · UI designs
## Three directions, every feature, three form factors
Each design is a clickable prototype covering the 5 existing tabs, a new cross-domain Today home, and all 17 existing sub-views (Tasks, Reminders, Notes, Habits, Growth · Code, Puzzles, Exams, DSA map · Spend, Budgets, Goals, Loans · Learn, Research, Watchlist · Agents). Switch design and device below, then click around inside the frame. All numbers are sample data.
## Choosing between them
Criterion | A · Command | B · Bento | C · Journal |
Core idea | Everything is a fast list you act on with keys | Everything is a glanceable tile you tap | Your day is one chronological page |
Strongest on | Desktop, power use, dense data (Money, Logic) | Phone, motivation, pets and streaks | iPad + Apple Pencil, reflection, notes |
Weakest on | Feels clinical; pets look out of place | Low information density; tiles need curation | Domain screens (Invest, Logic) are less scannable |
Build cost vs today | Low — mostly layout + palette, closest to current UI | Medium — tile system + new Home | High — timeline view merges 5 data keys by time |
Navigation model | Bottom tabs → rail → sidebar + ⌘K | Floating dock → top pills → vertical dock | Tabs → top text tabs → contents column |
New data it needs | None | XP / level derived from existing streaks | Per-item timestamps (partly exist) + day-level mood |
Suggestion: A's shell and B's Home are compatible — a hybrid (A navigation + B tiles on Home only) is the cheapest path that still fixes iPad and desktop. C is the most distinctive and the best home for the Pencil-notes idea in IDEAS.md, but is a bigger build.
Next step: pick a direction for each ask (delivery path in 2.1, sync v2 in 2.4, design A/B/C or a hybrid) and the build order in 2.7 becomes the plan. Sample data throughout; no live Forge data is read or sent by this page.
